criteria.quote: 0.1 kilos. Elephant down in two seconds.
criteria.revision: Replace the unsupported weight-led setup with the research-backed contradiction: “Gastly can topple an Indian elephant in two seconds—yet strong wind can quickly blow its gaseous body away.”

criteria.quote: an Indian elephant, in two seconds
How can something weighing 0.1 kilograms topple an elephant?
criteria.revision: Make the open question evidence-safe and more pointed: “How can something with no real shape envelop an opponent of any size—and what happens when strong wind hits it?”

criteria.quote: Gastly has no real shape because its body is gas. / That lets it envelop an opponent of any size. / Then the target gets specific: an Indian elephant, in two seconds.
criteria.revision: Replace the unsupported causal line and reduce repetition by escalating through the documented effects: “It has no real shape, but it can envelop an opponent of any size and cause suffocation. Inhaling part of its poisonous body can also cause one to faint instantly. Then the Pokédex names the target: an Indian elephant, toppled in two seconds.”

criteria.quote: But strong wind can quickly blow its gaseous body away.
criteria.revision: Use the sharper documented contrast without implying the threat is erased: “The same gaseous body quickly dwindles when exposed to strong wind.”

criteria.quote: A BODY MADE OF GAS / LARGE OR SMALL, IT CAN SURROUND THEM / THE POKÉDEX SETS A COUNTDOWN
criteria.revision: Replace the repeated gas-and-size beats with a distinct danger beat: “Inhaling part of its poisonous body causes one to faint instantly.” Keep the Indian-elephant countdown as the later scale reveal.

criteria.quote: Gastly turns a shapeless gas body into a threat against any size, with wind as its weakness.
criteria.revision: Resolve the contradiction with the strongest documented contrast: “Gastly needs no solid shape to envelop an opponent of any size and cause suffocation—but its gaseous body quickly dwindles in strong wind.”

criteria.quote: Overwhelming threat or fragile gas cloud?
criteria.revision: Make the two positions depend directly on the documented evidence: “Which defines Gastly better: a Pokémon that can envelop opponents of any size, or a gaseous body that strong wind can quickly blow away?”
